structured_output.analysis: Only one grid has been measured so far: iso_3.15, with KL=0.43614466651129274 [E514ab09c524e]. It already uses the full size budget. The layers where the loss concentrates already have their best method at their bit width: 27.up_proj and 2.up_proj on gptq_int3, and 3.up_proj, 1.up_proj and 27.gate_proj on rht_gptq_int3. So switching to another method at the same bit width gains nothing. Giving a layer more bits would need a matching downgrade elsewhere, but the evidence does not say which layers are at int4 or what each layer costs, so that move is risky this round. Changing GPTQ options keeps the bit count the same, so this round tests GPTQ options: act_order=true and lower damping.

proposals.name: iso_3.15_actorder
proposals.rationale: Changes options only, so the stored bits stay the same. In the base, KL=0.43614466651129274 [E514ab09c524e], and the largest single-layer losses are on GPTQ-quantized MLP layers: 27.up_proj gptq_int3 0.0057182 [Ef04d8aa7bded] and 14.down_proj rht_gptq_int2 0.00633466 [E4c3f9b73e065]. 27.up_proj has activation kurtosis 1090.09 [E24beed188b6a]. act_order=true quantizes the high-activation columns first, which should reduce the error they cause.

proposals.name: iso_3.15_actorder_damp005
proposals.rationale: Uses the same bits as the base (KL=0.43614466651129274 [E514ab09c524e]). Sets act_order=true and lowers damping from the default damp=0.01 to damp=0.005, so GPTQ follows the Hessian more closely. The losses are concentrated in MLP layers such as 3.up_proj rht_gptq_int3 0.0064177 [E6f4f7ea296d5] and 1.up_proj rht_gptq_int3 0.00611131 [E0564bc6ad1eb].

proposals.name: iso_3.15_damp005
proposals.rationale: Uses the same bits as the base (KL=0.43614466651129274 [E514ab09c524e]). Only lowers damping to damp=0.005, without act_order, so the effect of damping can be separated from act_order. The target is GPTQ error on layers such as 27.gate_proj rht_gptq_int3 0.00498703 [Efa0bb391da67] and 2.up_proj gptq_int3 0.00641875 [E9baa10763ebe].
